dedupe_keys.name: transxchange uk national xml standard for bus schedules and route registrations

description: TransXChange is the UK nationwide XML standard for exchanging bus schedules and related data, maintained by the Department for Transport. It is used both for the electronic registration of bus routes (EBSR) with the Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency and the Traffic Area Networks, and for passing routes and timetables to other systems such as journey planners and real-time vehicle tracking; operators' timetables in the Bus Open Data Service are published in this format. Coverage: Great Britain bus services; the downloads and schema page (published 12 March 2014) gives schema documentation for versions 2.1, 2.4 and 2.5, example documents and samples of real EBSR registrations, and the related UK standards NPTG, NaPTAN, JourneyWeb and CycleNetXChange, with Transmodel and NeTEx as the related European standards. A separate TXC Publisher desktop tool (guidance last updated 15 November 2016) renders TransXChange documents in readable form and runs integrity checks against business rules. Format and access: XML schemas referenced by URL or downloaded, with PDF guidance on GOV.UK; free. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): OGL-UK-3.0 (GOV.UK: all content under the Open Government Licence v3.0 unless otherwise stated). Caveats: the GOV.UK pages were last changed years ago and do not state the current schema version beyond 2.5; this is a format, and the timetable data themselves are separate records. Simulation uses: parsing operator timetables into transit network and service models for capacity planning and disruption studies. Related records: bus timetables in this format come from the Bus Open Data Service (data-uk-bus-open-data-service), stops from NaPTAN (data-uk-naptan), and the European counterpart is NeTEx (data-transmodel-netex-siri-standards).
